pages.text:
Abstract

We apply Grad-CAM to a DenseNet-121 classifier for chest X-ray diagnosis and study how saliency maps relate to predictions.

3 Methodology

Grad-CAM weights the feature maps of the last convolutional layer by pooled gradients to localize regions that drive a CNN prediction on chest X-ray images.

4 Results

DenseNet-121 achieved accuracy of 92.4% and AUROC of 0.951 on the ChestXray14 dataset.

5 Limitations

The saliency maps were not validated by radiologists. The maps are low resolution and can miss small lesions.

documents.title: Attention Rollout for Retinal Image Grading

pages.text:
Abstract

We study attention rollout for a vision transformer that grades diabetic retinopathy in fundus photographs.

4 Results

The ViT model reached accuracy of 88.1% on the EyePACS dataset. Attention rollout gave coarser maps than occlusion sensitivity.

5 Limitations

All images came from a single center, which limits generalization.

documents.title: Concept Bottleneck Models for Skin Lesion Classification

pages.text:
3 Methodology

A concept bottleneck model predicts clinically meaningful concepts first, then classifies skin lesions from those concepts, so each prediction is explained by concepts.

4 Results

The ResNet-50 concept model obtained F1 of 0.83 on the ISIC dataset.

5 Limitations

Concept annotations are expensive to collect. Future work will study automatic concept discovery.

documents.title: Counterfactual Explanations for Brain Tumor Segmentation

pages.text:
3 Methodology

We generate counterfactual explanations for a U-Net that segments brain tumors in MRI by perturbing the input until the segmentation changes.

4 Results

The U-Net reached Dice 0.87 on the BraTS dataset.

documents.title: Federated Averaging for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening

pages.text:
3 Methodology

FedAvg trains a shared model across hospitals without moving patient images, targeting diabetic retinopathy screening.
